Alongside those tools, proactively teaching the skill during calm moments — using puppets or dolls to re-enact a sharing conflict, reading books about characters who share and don't, and specifically praising good turn-taking when you catch it ("Sharing the play dough made you both happy") — builds the skill you want to see instead of only reacting once it breaks down. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.
